t: The Coordinating Committee of the Armed Forces, Police and Territorial Army, fewer than 110 privates, NCOs and junior officers, deposed Emperor Haile Selassie on 12 September 1974, killed sixty officials of his government on 23 November and abolished the monarchy in March 1975.

The Red Terror of 1976–1978 killed tens of thousands without trial, by the highest estimates up to 980,000, among them members of the rival Marxist-Leninist EPRP and MEISON; Mengistu Haile Mariam, chairman after the shootout of 3 February 1977, intensified it.

The famine of 1983–85, which the Derg itself estimated at more than a million deaths, was deliberately worsened in the rebel areas of Tigray and Eritrea as a counter-insurgency strategy, and the regime's enforced resettlement killed between 50,000 and 100,000 more.
dyk: The Derg was said to have 120 members at its founding in 1974, in fact fewer than 110, and it never admitted a new one; by 1980 expulsions and killings had reduced it to 38, all but three of them Amhara.
ev: The Derg is established as the Coordinating Committee of the Armed Forces, Police and Territorial Army by junior and mid-level officers; announced on 28 June, it elects Major Mengistu Haile Mariam chairman.
On 12 September the Derg deposes and imprisons Emperor Haile Selassie during nationwide protests; three days later it renames itself the Provisional Military Administrative Council.
On 23 November the Derg removes and kills its chairman, Lieutenant General Aman Andom, with some of his supporters and 60 officials of the imperial government, the Massacre of the Sixty.
On 4 March the land reform 'Land to the Tiller' nationalises all rural land and abolishes tenancy; the monarchy is formally abolished the same month, and Haile Selassie dies on 27 August.
On 23 September the Red Terror begins after a failed attempt on Mengistu's life attributed to the EPRP; in less than two years up to 980,000 people are killed by the highest estimates.
On 3 February Chairman Tafari Benti is killed in a shootout and Mengistu takes power; Vice-Chairman Atnafu Abate is executed with 40 officers on 13 November; Somalia invades the Ogaden.
Famine in northern Ethiopia, multiplied by the government's policies in the rebel regions, kills about 1.2 million people; Live Aid raises money in July 1985.

On 22 February the Derg government ends after a referendum approves the constitution of the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia; the Derg is formally abolished in September, its members keeping power.

f.founder: Junior and mid-level officers of the Imperial Ethiopian Army and the police, who elected Major Mengistu Haile Mariam chairman; Lieutenant General Aman Andom was its first head of state
f.predecessor: The Ethiopian Empire of Emperor Haile Selassie, deposed on 12 September 1974
f.successor: People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (1987–1991), led by the Workers' Party of Ethiopia under Mengistu; overthrown by the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front in May 1991
